identity.title: ALMA reveals a large structured disk and nested rotating outflows in DG Tauri B

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) Band 6 observations at 14-20 au spatial resolution of the disk and CO(2-1) outflow around the Class I protostar DG Tau B in Taurus.

question.value: What are the structure and kinematics of the DG Tau B disk and of its CO(2-1) outflow, and do the rotating conical outflow walls trace the interface with infalling material or material ejected from the disk?

evidence.quote: Studies at high-angular and spectral resolution of objects with weak or no infalling envelopes with ALMA are crucial to help discriminate between an envelope and a disk origin for the rotating outflow material.

findings_qualitative.value: Inner conical outflow shows hollow cone with shear-like velocity structure, coincident with scattered light cavity

findings_qualitative.value: A wider slower outflow component surrounds the cone and also rotates with the disk

claims.hypothesis: Large structured disks can form at an early stage with ongoing infall
claims.experiment: Band 6 continuum and 13CO imaging with profile fitting
claims.result: R_eff95=174 au, CO radius 700 au, bumps at 62 and 135 au, Keplerian rotation
claims.finding: Large structured disk exists around Class I DG Tau B

evidence.quote: These results confirm that large structured disks can form at an early stage where residual infall is still ongoing.

claims.hypothesis: The conical CO outflow walls rotate and carry significant mass
claims.experiment: 12CO channel maps, transverse PV cuts and LTE mass flux
claims.result: Delta V=1 km/s at 120 au, j~65 au km/s, mass flux 1.7-2.9e-7 Msun/yr
claims.finding: Cone rotates with the disk and carries 35x the jet mass flux

evidence.quote: We confirm their global average rotation in the same sense as the disk, with a specific angular momentum $\simeq$ 65 au km s$^{-1}$.

claims.hypothesis: The cone walls trace the interface between infall and outflow
claims.experiment: Compare wide low-velocity component with Ulrich infall models
claims.result: No infall parameters reproduce the wide component

evidence.quote: do not trace the interface with infalling material, which is shown to be confined to much wider angles ($> 70^{\circ}$)
